title: What gambling training do NSW hotel and club gaming staff need?
seoTitle: NSW RCG and ARCG training rules
description: Who needs NSW Responsible Conduct of Gambling training, the ARCG rule for RGOs and managers, Responsible Gambling Officer numbers and the 5 year refresher.
shortAnswer: In New South Wales, anyone whose duties involve gaming machines, including staff who patrol or serve in a gaming area, must complete Responsible Conduct of Gambling (RCG) training with a Liquor & Gaming NSW approved provider and hold the endorsement on an NSW competency card. Responsible Gambling Officers, licensees, managers and club directors need Advanced RCG. Venues with more than 20 gaming machine entitlements must roster Responsible Gambling Officers whenever machines operate.
keyTakeaways: RCG is mandatory for staff who patrol or serve in a gaming machine area and, from June 30, 2025, for club directors (unless they completed Responsible Gambling Board Oversight training) and operational directors of hotel owning companies.
A new RCG candidate must pass a 25 question online assessment, answering every question correctly, before receiving a 90 day interim certificate.
The RCG endorsement must be renewed every five years through an online refresher, and Liquor & Gaming NSW sends a reminder 90 days before expiry.

Advanced RCG (ARCG) is required for Responsible Gambling Officers, Responsible Gambling Managers, hotel licensees, approved managers, club secretaries and gaming supervisors in venues with any number of machines.

Since July 1, 2024 the Gaming Machines Regulation 2019 requires one to three Responsible Gambling Officers on duty, depending on entitlements, in every hotel and club with more than 20 gaming machine entitlements.
jurisdiction: Australia (New South Wales): Gaming Machines Act 2001 and Gaming Machines Regulation 2019
appliesTo: Hotel and club staff who patrol or serve in a gaming machine area
Responsible Gambling Officers and Responsible Gambling Managers
Hotel licensees, approved managers and club secretaries

Approved training providers delivering RCG, ARCG and RGBO courses

sections.heading: Who must complete RCG training in NSW?

blocks.text: RCG training is mandatory for anyone whose work duties involve gaming machines in New South Wales. Liquor & Gaming NSW's [RCG page](https://www.nsw.gov.au/business-and-economy/liquor-and-gaming/training/responsible-conduct-gambling) lists the groups covered: staff who patrol or serve in a gaming machine area, directors of registered clubs with gaming machines, directors of companies owning hotels with gaming machines who are involved in hotel operations, and anyone planning to enroll in Advanced RCG.

The director requirements applied from June 30, 2025. Club directors can meet them either through RCG plus ARCG or through the shorter Responsible Gambling Board Oversight (RGBO) course. The regulator explains that RCG and ARCG are established under the Gaming Machines Act 2001 and the Gaming Machines Regulation 2019 and are therefore focused on gaming machines rather than other forms of gambling such as TAB or Keno.

RCG sits on the same NSW competency card as Responsible Service of Alcohol (RSA). The card mechanics, including how multiple endorsements share one expiry date, are covered on the [NSW RSA competency card page](/regulations/responsible-service-of-alcohol-training-nsw); this page covers what is specific to gaming.

sections.heading: What does the RCG course cover, and how is it assessed?

blocks.text: The RCG course covers gambling in Australia and NSW, defining and understanding gambling harm, responsible gambling and harm minimization measures, interacting with patrons using the "RAAR" framework, and responsible conduct of gambling in practice. It is only available through Liquor & Gaming NSW approved training providers, in a classroom or virtually.

Assessment is centralized. After the provider lodges the course, Liquor & Gaming NSW emails and texts the candidate a link to an online assessment of 25 questions, mostly multiple choice and multiple answer. The candidate has unlimited attempts at each question but must answer all 25 correctly to pass. Only then is the RCG interim certificate issued, and the interim certificate is what allows a person to start gaming duties.

items: Complete the RCG course with an approved training provider, which lodges the completion with Liquor & Gaming NSW.
Complete the 25 question online assessment sent by Liquor & Gaming NSW, answering every question correctly.
Receive the interim certificate by email, valid for 90 days, and start gaming duties.
Take the interim certificate and 100 points of identification to a Service NSW center for a proof of identity check to obtain the competency card, including the digital version.

blocks.title: Onboarding risk
blocks.text: There is no time limit on completing the online assessment, and Liquor & Gaming NSW sends no reminders. A new hire who finishes the course but not the assessment has no interim certificate and cannot lawfully perform gaming duties. Rosters should key off the interim certificate date, not the course date.

sections.heading: How often must RCG be refreshed?

blocks.text: The RCG endorsement must be renewed every five years by completing the online RCG Refresher course before the competency card expires. Liquor & Gaming NSW notifies holders by email or phone 90 days before expiry, provided their contact details are current.

The refresher covers the Australian and NSW gambling environment, problem and at risk gambling, legal and ethical responsibilities of staff, and staff interactions with patrons. Holders with a digital card see the competency update automatically once the refresher is complete. The ARCG endorsement is renewed automatically when the RCG refresher is completed before the card expires, so an RGO who lets RCG lapse also loses the advanced endorsement.

Because the regulator's reminder depends on contact details it holds, venues should not rely on it. A venue level register of each staff member's card expiry, reviewed monthly, is the control an inspector would expect. [How to set mandatory training refresh cycles](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles) covers how to build that schedule.

sections.heading: Who needs Advanced RCG or board oversight training?

blocks.text: Advanced Responsible Conduct of Gambling (ARCG) is mandatory for Responsible Gambling Officers and for people in senior operational roles in hotels and clubs with gaming machines. RCG must be completed first. The [ARCG page](https://www.nsw.gov.au/business-and-economy/liquor-and-gaming/training/advanced-responsible-conduct-of-gambling) and the regulator's RGO guidance list hotel licensees, approved managers as defined in section 91(1A) of the Liquor Act 2007, club secretaries, club directors who have not done RGBO, operational directors of hotel owning companies, staff who supervise gaming operations and RGOs, and Responsible Gambling Managers.

ARCG covers managing complex patron interactions, using behavioral models to support decisions, ethical decisions where legislation gives no clear answer, and designing and managing harm minimization systems. It includes separate learning for gaming operations staff and for venue leadership.

The [RGBO course](https://www.nsw.gov.au/business-and-economy/liquor-and-gaming/training/rgbo) is a one hour condensed version of ARCG for club directors. Liquor & Gaming NSW extended the deadline for club directors from December 31, 2024 to June 30, 2025. RGBO does not add an endorsement to the competency card; directors must keep the provider's completion certificate as proof, which places the record keeping burden on the club rather than the card system.

sections.heading: How many Responsible Gambling Officers must a venue roster?

blocks.text: Every hotel and club with more than 20 gaming machine entitlements must have Responsible Gambling Officers (RGOs) on duty whenever gaming machines are operating, and each RGO must hold ARCG. Liquor & Gaming NSW's [RGO guidance](https://www.nsw.gov.au/business-and-economy/liquor-and-gaming/gaming/responsible-gaming/responsible-gambling-officer) says that from July 1, 2024 the Regulation's RGO requirements override gaming related license conditions on RGOs.

blocks.text: RGOs monitor gaming areas, support staff with gambling related concerns, facilitate self exclusion and maintain and review the Gambling Incident Register. A venue running far fewer machines than its entitlement can apply for a variation, granted for 12 months only and revoked immediately if more machines operate than the variation allows. A Responsible Gambling Manager supervises RGOs under clause 50G of the Regulation and must also hold ARCG. Penalties for breaching RGO and Gambling Incident Register requirements are listed in Schedule 4 of the Regulation.

sections.heading: What penalties apply to gambling training breaches?

blocks.text: Penalty notices apply both to venues and to training providers. The regulator's [competency card fines page](https://www.nsw.gov.au/business-and-economy/liquor-and-gaming/training/competency-cards/fines) lists RCG related penalties of $2,750 for an organization and $550 for an individual for providing an RCG course without approval, advertising an unapproved course, granting an interim certificate without course completion, or breaching approval conditions, referencing sections 49B to 49D of the Gaming Machines Act 2001 and Schedule 4 of the Regulation.

Liquor & Gaming NSW says it takes an educational or remedial approach to low risk matters and stronger action, including penalty notices, prosecution and license conditions, for more serious ones. As at November 2026, venues should treat the RGO roster and the Gambling Incident Register as the two records most likely to be examined during a gaming inspection.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry links each venue role to the endorsement it requires and to the venue's entitlement count, so the RGO obligation and the director training route follow from the venue's own data. Card expiry dates are tracked per person, with the ARCG dependency on the RCG refresher made explicit.

faqs.q: Can a new gaming attendant start work straight after the RCG course?
faqs.a: Only after passing the online assessment and receiving the RCG interim certificate. Liquor & Gaming NSW issues the assessment after the provider lodges the course, and all 25 questions must be answered correctly. The interim certificate, valid for 90 days, is what allows a person to work in duties involving gaming machines.

faqs.q: Does a venue with 15 gaming machines need a Responsible Gambling Officer?
faqs.a: No. The RGO requirement applies to hotels and clubs with more than 20 gaming machine entitlements. However, in venues with any number of gaming machines, the hotel licensee, approved managers, club secretary, club directors (unless they did RGBO) and operational directors of hotel owning companies must still complete ARCG.

faqs.q: Do club directors have to hold an RCG competency card?
faqs.a: Club directors of venues with gaming machines must complete either RCG plus ARCG, which appear on the competency card, or the one hour RGBO course, which does not. Directors who choose RGBO must keep the approved training provider's completion certificate as proof. The deadline for directors was June 30, 2025.

faqs.q: Can security staff act as Responsible Gambling Officers?
faqs.a: Liquor & Gaming NSW does not recommend it, because a security guard is unlikely to be able to discharge RGO duties and security obligations at the same time. Existing gaming attendants, duty managers or supervisors can be RGOs if they hold ARCG and have the capacity and proximity to the gaming area to perform the role.
